subject: AegisPay transit processors — scope confirmation & supporting artifacts
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alistair Wong <awong@aegispay.com>, compliance@aegispay.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: AegisPay transit processors — scope confirmation & supporting artifacts

Hi Alistair / AegisPay compliance team,

Thanks for the productive call last week. As part of the DPA amendment review we need a concise list of any third parties that process transit or routing of customer content on your behalf (examples: CDN partners, edge proxies, log shippers, gateway providers). Specifically we need:

- canonical name of the processor
- primary function (e.g., CDN, object store, logging)
- countries where they operate or store data
- whether they act as a subprocessor (yes/no)
- link to their latest SOC2 / ISO evidence or equivalent
- IP ranges or FQDNs we should allow for peering/firewall rules

I've attached a simple inventory template (aegispay-processor-inventory-template.csv) — if you can fill that out and return by end of week it would keep our security review on track. Also, if any of the processors will be added to your roster in the next 30–60 days please flag them so we can start contract-side work (amendment / DocuSign).

Two quick asks from our side:
1) If EdgeRoute (or any CDN) caches request bodies or parsed content, call that out explicitly.
2) Provide the geographic regions for data transit (US east/west, EU, APAC) — that impacts our routing policy and any contractual cross-border language.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a short call if easier.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Compliance & Risk
Redwood Inference

Attachment: aegispay-processor-inventory-template.csv (CSV stub)

From: Alistair Wong <awong@aegispay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@aegispay.com, legal@aegispay.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AegisPay transit processors — scope confirmation & supporting artifacts

Hi Kimberly — thanks for the note and the template.

I attached a completed inventory (aegispay-processor-inventory-completed.csv) and a quick dataflow PNG that shows where each partner sits. High level:
- EdgeRoute (CDN / edge caching) — caches static assets only; operates US, EU, APAC.
- StoreBox (object store for telemetry snapshots) — stores encrypted blobs; primary region US East, occasional cross-border replication to EU for DR.
- LogShip (log forwarding) — forwards sanitized access logs to our analytics pipeline; US-only.

Regarding evidence: EdgeRoute has a SOC2 report (link in CSV), StoreBox provides ISO/Attestation docs, LogShip supplied a vendor security questionnaire. For IP ranges, I included a column in the CSV with FQDNs and published ranges where available.

Two clarifications from our legal team: if Redwood requires subprocessor-level signatures (amendments) we can do a single omnibus addendum for the roster or route through our vendor portal for individual consent. Which do you prefer?

We can get any missing artifacts over the next 48 hours.

Thanks,
Alistair Wong
Head of Platform Operations
AegisPay Inc.

Attachments: aegispay-processor-inventory-completed.csv, dataflow-diagram-v2.png

Hi Alistair — appreciate the fast turnaround and the diagram. A few follow-ups after a quick review: 

- EdgeRoute caching: you note "static assets only" — can you confirm whether any request/response bodies (even partial) are cached for more than 60 seconds? That affects whether we consider them to be processing customer content.
- StoreBox replication to EU: we need to confirm whether the replication is customer-specific or metadata-only. If customer blobs replicate cross-border and are decryptable by StoreBox staff, we will need the EU transfer mechanism documented (SCCs or equivalent).
- LogShip: confirm retention window for forwarded logs and whether logs contain any PII or prompt snippets.

For the amendment vs. omnibus question: to keep procurement friction low for both sides, Redwood prefers an omnibus addendum that lists the roster with a single signature from AegisPay. That lets us keep the DPA appendices in sync. If your legal prefers the portal, we can accept that too — but we need a clear timeline for when the roster will be finalized.

Do you have SOC2/ISO zip files? If so please upload to the Drive link I shared (or paste direct links). If you can get the missing items by EOW (Fri, Oct 2) that will keep us on schedule for the customer's review next week.

Thanks — Kim

Kim / Rishi — forwarding for visibility. A few internal asks based on Alistair's inventory: 

- Can Security validate whether EdgeRoute's caching behavior would flag them as a processor of customer payloads? If yes, we need to add them to the DPA roster immediately.
- Procurement: if we go omnibus, let's prepare an amendment template that includes an annex with processor roles and a signature block. I can draft a first pass and loop Legal (Laura) for redlines.
- Ops: Rishi, please add the FQDNs from the CSV to our allowlist proposal and confirm whether any of them require peering (rather than public egress).

Also flagging that StoreBox's cross-border replication could change our SCCs assessment — if StoreBox staff can access plaintext for DR, we need SCCs or documented transfer mechanism before production traffic flows through their pipeline.

I'll plan to send a draft amendment to AegisPay by Thu morning unless Security asks for more evidence.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kim / Marissa / team — quick update and attachments: 

- EdgeRoute: confirmed no caching of request bodies longer than 30s. Static assets only. SOC2 link: https://edge-route.example.com/soc2-report.pdf (also in CSV).
- StoreBox: replication is metadata-only for the customer snapshots we retain for 7 days. For DR, selected encrypted snapshots are replicated to EU; StoreBox team confirms they cannot decrypt without AegisPay-managed KMS keys. They provided an attestation PDF (attached) and IP ranges.
- LogShip: retention 14 days, sanitized; no prompt-level PII in forwarded logs per supplier questionnaire.

Per our legal team we prepared an omnibus addendum and uploaded it to DocuSign for your review: https://app.docusign.com/recipient/SigningPreview?doc=0a1b2c3d4e — the addendum includes the processor roster and the standard amendment language.
